join_order.notes: Resolve k_id (scan keyword/keyword varlen). Drive query from small CSR slice of mk rows for k_id.
Dense PK on title: lookup t_ep[mv-1] per mk row. No prebuilt set; per-row predicate check.
Build bitset cn_us_bs over company_name rows (~30% of 234997). For each surviving movie, scan mc offsets and require any mc.company_id with cn_us_bs set.
For each qualifying movie, enumerate ci rows; collect ci.person_id.
name.id is dense PK so n.id = ci.person_id is automatic; per pid, enumerate an rows.

filters.predicate: episode_nr != NULL AND episode_nr >= 5 AND episode_nr < 100

parallelism.notes: Partition mk_k_row[lo..hi) across 12 threads; each thread maintains thread-local min for an.name and t.title; final reduction merges by lexicographic min. Use std::string_view comparisons keyed off (name.off, name.dat) and (title.off, title.dat).

execution_notes: Step A: scan company_name/country_code.dict to find dict id for '[us]' => us_code (int16).
Step B: scan keyword/keyword varlen for exact match 'character-name-in-title' => k_id (int32).
Step C: build bitset cn_us_bs[r] = (cn_country_code[r] == us_code) over 234997 rows.
Step D: lo=mk_k_off[k_id], hi=mk_k_off[k_id+1]; for r in [lo,hi): mv = mk_k_row[r].
Step E: if !t_ep_ok(mv-1) continue. mv_idx = mv-1.
Step F: mc_lo=mc_off[mv_idx], mc_hi=mc_off[mv_idx+1]; us_ok=false; for j in [mc_lo,mc_hi) if cn_us_bs[mc_company_id[j]-1] { us_ok=true; break; }; if !us_ok continue.
Step G: update local min_t_title with title varlen(mv-1).
Step H: ci_lo=ci_off[mv_idx], ci_hi=ci_off[mv_idx+1]; for j in [ci_lo,ci_hi): pid = ci_person_id[j].
Step I: an_lo=an_off[pid-1], an_hi=an_off[pid-1+1]; for a in [an_lo,an_hi): update local min_an_name with aka_name varlen(a).
Step J: parallel reduce thread-local mins → final two scalars.
